title: Refactor policy adapter and simplify regional fallback topology
creator: Aisha Cohen
description: This ticket consolidates several small tech-debt tangles in the smart routing layer: (1) extract a lean policy-adapter interface that isolates policy evaluation from transport-layer concerns, (2) remove the legacy global region mutex and migrate regional affinity decisions to an asynchronous evented path, and (3) simplify fallback topology by delaminating fallback decision logic from per-request hotpaths. Goal: reduce tail latency variance and lock contention during high burst traffic while keeping deterministic fallback semantics for SLA-backed customers.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce PolicyAdapter v2 interface with clear separation of evaluatePolicy(requestContext) and subscribeAffinityChanges(cb)
All existing policy logic migrated off the global mutex; no routes under /api/router/* should take global locks in production traces (verified by sampling traces)
End-to-end latency p95 for routing decisions improves by at least 20% under the synthetic surge workload (see benchmark instructions)
Fallback decisions are taken via the new fallback executor and can be re-played in a dry-run mode for 30 days after rollout
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering 95% of the new modules, and e2e test in staging with regression dataset (link in links)
Migration plan documented and rollback safe: traffic can be cut back to legacy policy path via runtime flag per-region
implementation_steps: Design & API: draft PolicyAdapter v2 (small interface) and publish to confluence (doc link)
Prototype: implement in staging runtime with feature flag 'policy_adpt_v2' and internal canary 10% of routing traffic
Benchmark: run surge benchmark harness (see links) to compare p50/p95 and lock contention metrics
Refactor: move fallback decision tree into FallbackExecutor which handles backoff/circuit logic asynchronously
Hardening: add telemetry (histograms for decision latency, counter for fallback type counts, gauges for region-leases)
Rollout: staged ramp by region (NA-eu-apac) using runtime flags, monitor SLOs and canary alerts
Cleanup: remove legacy codepaths and global region mutex after 2 weeks of stable metrics
decisions: Use a thin PolicyAdapter v2 boundary to make future language/runtime ports easier (Go -> Rust possibility)
FallbackExecutor will be single-writer per-region but not global; region shard selection uses consistent hashing
Telemetry will include decision_trace_id for correlating policy decisions with user-facing latency
We will keep legacy path togglable for 30 days and use dry-run mode to validate parity
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: RFC posted to #infra-routing and confluence. Initial feedback asks for clearer metrics (added histogram buckets).
2026-03-04: Prototype PolicyAdapter v2 committed behind feature flag (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5234). Scoped to NA region for canary.
2026-03-06: Discovered a subtle ordering bug when migrating KV cache invalidation — reverted that portion and added deterministic unit test to reproduce.

2026-03-08: Benchmarks in staging harness show p95 routing-decision latency reduced 22% at 2k rps surge; lock-wait syscalls reduced by ~38% (dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ routing/lock-contention)
2026-03-10: Code review feedback from Lucia Park requesting clearer invariants for 'fallback preemption' — added decision matrix and updated PR.
